summary: The most probable root cause is that auth-kyc's outbound connection to the external kyc-provider is being refused. From 09:55 UTC auth-kyc logs 'kyc vendor connection refused: tcp connect to kyc-provider failed', roughly half of KYC calls fail, and orchestrator receives HTTP 503s from auth-kyc, which blocks signup and KYC. Orchestrator's errors and latency are a downstream effect of this, not an independent fault. The postgres 09:13 deploy, the llm-gateway latency and the late auth-kyc 10:48 deploy look like red herrings or are ruled out as triggers. The exact reason for the refusal (vendor outage, changed endpoint/port, DNS or egress config) is not established, so the next step is to check the vendor side and auth-kyc's egress path.

hypotheses.statement: auth-kyc's outbound connection to the external kyc-provider is being refused (vendor endpoint down, or a changed endpoint, port, DNS or egress/firewall config), so roughly half of KYC calls fail and return 503 to orchestrator, which blocks signup and KYC.
hypotheses.label: high

supporting.text: auth-kyc err_rate was at baseline in the 09:50 bucket and jumped to about 0.54 in the 09:55 bucket, plateauing near 0.60, which matches the reported onset.
The first auth-kyc ERROR is at 09:55:40Z and names kyc-provider as the refused connection target. All 13 ERROR lines in the window carry the identical message, and there were no errors before it.
Successful status checks stop short of a full outage, so the failure is partial, consistent with roughly half of calls failing.
auth-kyc latency stepped up at 09:55 (about 136 ms to about 528 ms) with no rise in request volume, consistent with a dependency problem rather than load.
Orchestrator errors begin at 09:55:20Z and every orchestrator ERROR line names an HTTP 503 from auth-kyc, so orchestrator is a downstream victim and signup/KYC blocking follows from this.

It is likely that the failure is on the path to the external vendor (vendor endpoint down, or network/DNS/firewall/port change), because the error is a TCP refusal and not an auth or DB error. This is inferred from the message text and not confirmed.

contradicting.text: The logs show only the client-side view of the refusal. Vendor status, resolved address, and whether the endpoint or port changed were not observed, so the underlying reason is unconfirmed.

The topology lists no callees for auth-kyc and kyc-provider is not a modelled dependency, so the external edge cannot be confirmed from the graph. If a library or unmodelled config makes the call, that would explain the gap, but this is unverified.

No config, migration or flag change is recorded near onset that would explain a changed endpoint, so a trigger on our side is not visible. The change tool may not capture infra, DNS or egress changes.

hypotheses.statement: A silent non-deploy event on the auth-kyc side, such as a KYC provider credential or TLS certificate expiry, or a scheduled job, started at 09:55 and makes the vendor connection fail intermittently.
hypotheses.label: low

contradicting.text: No credential or database error messages appear at ERROR level for auth-kyc. The dominant error is a refused TCP connection, which does not look like a credential or certificate failure.

No credential, token or certificate change is visible in the change history. This does not rule out silent expiry, since expiry is not a recorded change, so H2 is weakly unsupported rather than excluded. It is likely at most a possible cause of a failed vendor connection, and it can coexist with H1.

facts.text: auth-kyc err_rate was at baseline (0.003) in the 5-minute bucket just before onset.
auth-kyc err_rate jumped to 0.543 in the 09:55 bucket, matching the reported onset.
auth-kyc err_rate reached about 0.60 by 10:00 and stayed there through the end of the window.
auth-kyc's only listed dependency is a caller, orchestrator, with call weight 0.1; no synchronous callees were returned.
First auth-kyc ERROR in the 09:50-10:05 window; the message names kyc-provider as the failing connection target.
The same connection-refused ERROR recurs through the window; the last one in the result is at 10:04:53Z. I count 13 ERROR lines of this message in T6-01 (total 15 WARN+ lines, 2 of them WARN).
Before the first error, the INFO-level result shows only successful KYC status checks (no errors in 09:50:00-09:55:11Z).

Successful status checks continue after onset, so the failure is partial (roughly half of logged KYC activity errors), not a complete outage. This weakens any claim that all auth-kyc processing is down.
Orchestrator err_rate was at baseline in the 09:50 bucket and jumped in the 09:55 bucket, the same bucket as the auth-kyc onset, not before it.
auth-kyc latency_ms stepped up at 09:55, from about 136 ms to about 528 ms, the same bucket as the orchestrator change.
auth-kyc rps shows no step at onset; it stays around 15 across 09:50 to 10:25, so the latency rise is not explained by a request-volume increase.
Orchestrator ERROR logs have no entries from 09:45 until 09:55:00. The first is at 09:55:20Z.
Every orchestrator ERROR line in the 09:45 to 10:05 window names auth-kyc as the failing downstream call. None names llm-gateway or any other dependency. The result is not truncated and has 38 lines.

get_dependencies for auth-kyc returns only one edge, a caller (orchestrator, weight 0.1). No callees are listed, so auth-kyc's dependencies on postgres, redis-cache and the KYC provider are not shown.

The change query covered deploy, config, migration and flag kinds across all services for 09:00-11:00. It returned 3 records, none truncated or partial. All three are deploys, so no config, migration or flag change is recorded in the window.
All 13 ERROR lines in the window have the identical message, so no other error code or message dominates.
No ERROR lines appear between 09:50 and 09:55:40, which matches the metric onset in the 09:55 bucket.
No credential or database error messages were returned for auth-kyc at ERROR level in this window.

The only change recorded for auth-kyc in the 08:00–11:00 window, across deploy, config, migration and flag kinds, is a deploy at 10:48, after the 09:55 onset. No auth-kyc config, migration or flag change appears near onset.

assumptions.text: 'Connection refused' at TCP level usually means the target actively rejected the connection or nothing was listening on that host and port. It points to the provider endpoint, its port, or local egress/DNS config rather than a slow or timed-out provider. This is inferred from the message text, not confirmed.
No auth-kyc or KYC-provider credential, token or certificate change is visible in the change history for 09:00-11:00, but this does not rule out silent expiry, since expiry is not a recorded change.

The failure is probably on the path to the external KYC vendor (network, DNS, firewall, or the vendor endpoint being down), since the error is a connection refusal and not an auth or DB error. Dependency or deploy data is needed to confirm this.
auth-kyc's external provider call is probably made through a library or config that the service topology does not model. That would explain why no external edge appears, but I have not verified it.

unresolved: The reason for the refusal is unconfirmed: vendor outage, changed endpoint/port, DNS or egress/firewall config. The vendor side and its own status were not queried.
kyc-provider is not in the service list and the topology shows no callees for auth-kyc, so the dependency is unmodelled and its host and port are unknown.
Logs were only queried for 09:50-10:05, so it is unknown whether errors continue or have stopped. The metrics show the plateau through the end of the window.
It is unknown whether existing customers are also affected; log lines carry no customer-type field.
Signup-path logs for orchestrator and wa-webhook were not queried, so the link to the signup flow is inferred from orchestrator's 503s.
Credential, token and certificate expiry and scheduled jobs could not be checked with the available tools, so H2 is not fully excluded.
The postgres-00185 deploy diff was unavailable (source and url null), so 'label rename only' is unverified; it is treated as unlikely to be related.
The earlier 'timeout' log query returned nothing, probably because the failure text is 'connection refused', so it is not evidence of no failures.
The llm-gateway latency of about 1.4 s is flat across onset and likely unrelated; no baseline is available, and no llm-gateway error logs were queried.
RabbitMQ queue health and msg-delivery were not checked, so undelivered KYC/OTP messages are unverified.
Some summary statistics differ slightly from plotted points and between calls (e.g. orchestrator err_rate max 0.065 vs 0.064), probably because of raw versus downsampled data.
No query_logs calls were made, so error codes, messages and the failing signup or KYC steps are unknown.
No endpoint, error-type or new-versus-existing customer breakdown was obtained; I cannot say whether existing customers are affected.
auth-kyc latency_ms and rps were only summarized (no points), so their timing relative to the err_rate step is unverified.
wa-webhook, orchestrator and web-app were only summarized; their latency and error timing against 09:55 is unknown, and the orchestrator err_rate spike has no time attached.
Tool budget (about 5 calls) was reached, so the sampling resolution of 5 minutes limits the precision of onset timing.

Summary-only metric calls return no points, so onset relative to 09:55 could not be determined for any metric. Points with step_min are needed for postgres pool/slow queries, redis hit_ratio, and llm-gateway latency.
No rabbitmq queue depth, consumer count, consumer lag, redelivery or dead-letter metrics were returned for inbound-msgs, outbound-msgs or portfolio-updates. Queue health is unverified.

The auth-kyc query was limited to WARN+ with the term 'timeout'. External KYC provider timeouts may be logged under other terms or at a different level, so the zero result is not proof of no timeouts.
Postgres locks and error logs, and redis timeout logs, were not queried. Only metric summaries were collected for those services.
Baseline values for llm-gateway latency are not available, so calling 1.4 s elevated is an inference from the other services' scale, not a measured deviation.
Call budget (5 calls) was used on summaries and one log query, so no follow-up was possible.

Change history only covers deploy, config, migration and flag kinds. Cache expiry, scheduled jobs, certificate or token expiry, infra or scaling changes, and third-party credential or provider changes were not checked and may not be captured by the tool.

Only one change query was run across all services, with no per-service confirmation for auth-kyc, wa-webhook, orchestrator, web-app, redis-cache, rabbitmq or llm-gateway. The global result was not truncated or partial, so it is treated as complete but is not independently confirmed.
No flag or config entries scoped to new-user or onboarding flows appeared in the results. This could be real or a gap in what the tool records.
get_dependencies returned no callees for auth-kyc, which is unexpected for a KYC service. The topology data may be incomplete, so the downstream blast radius is unverified.
The lookback started at 00:00 UTC, so changes earlier than that, or scheduled jobs running on longer cycles, are not covered.
auth-kyc shows no outgoing calls, so its external KYC providers and any postgres or redis dependency are unverified.
rabbitmq returned no edges, so inbound-msgs and outbound-msgs producers and consumers are unverified beyond orchestrator's links.
wa-webhook, msg-delivery, web-app, redis-cache and postgres were not queried because of the call budget.
The change query returned only deploys; no config, migration or flag changes appeared in the window, which weakens non-deploy triggers but does not rule them out.
order-router and aa-sync do not appear in orchestrator's edges, so their link to onboarding is unknown.
Past incidents were not searched, so no historical analogues were checked.

Searches for 'new user signup KYC failure onboarding stall' and 'onboarding postgres redis-cache rabbitmq outage signup' returned zero items, and 'KYC' alone also returned zero. Search is keyword-based, so an incident titled differently (for example 'identity', 'verification' or 'registration') could be missed.
Past incidents give dates but no service or UTC timestamps, so their timing cannot be compared with the 09:55 UTC onset.
I found no past incident showing postgres or rabbitmq affecting onboarding. This is not proof there was none, since search was limited to 3 queries.
No incident that first looked like one cause and turned out to be another was returned; the results do not allow that comparison.
No HTTP or status codes appear in any auth-kyc line; the failure is a TCP connect error, so the status-code part of the request cannot be answered from these logs.
No exception class or stack trace is logged; the message is a plain string.
kyc-provider is not in the services list and has no IP address or port in the message, so its exact host and port are unknown. Its own logs were not queried.

The log lines carry no customer-type field, and error lines name no user ID. I cannot tell from these results whether only new customers are affected or existing customers also see the errors (the 'kyc status check ok' user IDs are not classified).
Only the 09:50-10:05 window was queried at WARN+ and INFO. I did not check for errors before 09:50 or after 10:05, so I cannot confirm the exact start or whether errors have stopped.
Signup-path logs for orchestrator and wa-webhook were not queried in this task, so I cannot link these auth-kyc errors to the signup flow directly.

5-minute bucket averages cannot show whether orchestrator or auth-kyc moved first within the 09:55 bucket. The first orchestrator error log at 09:55:20Z is consistent with auth-kyc leading, but this needs auth-kyc's own logs, which I did not query.

The summary stats for these metrics do not match the plotted points. Orchestrator latency max is 1013.943 but the highest point is 963.544. auth-kyc latency max is 588.622 but the highest point is 566.35. llm-gateway latency max is 1467.635 but the highest point is 1414.674. The stats probably cover raw samples, while points are downsampled.

auth-kyc has no listed outgoing edges (per E-023), so the dependency graph cannot confirm kyc-provider as a modelled dependency. Config or deploy changes to the KYC endpoint need checking by the dependency agent.

No external KYC or identity provider is named in any tool result, so the provider could not be identified.

No tool reports provider-side status, outage notices, certificate or credential expiry, or rate-limit data, so none of those three possibilities can be confirmed or ruled out for 09:55.
Past-incident search (INC-0388) is only a hint. The search index has no record of KYC or identity-provider incidents, so the historical record gives no basis for a known cause.

actions.text: Check the kyc-provider's status page/vendor contact and test TCP connectivity (DNS resolution, host and port) to the KYC vendor from an auth-kyc host.
actions.rationale: The error is a refused TCP connect to kyc-provider starting at 09:55:40Z; confirming whether the endpoint is down or changed separates vendor outage from our egress or DNS config.

actions.text: If a secondary or fallback KYC provider or endpoint exists, fail over to it, or enable retries with backoff on auth-kyc's vendor calls, to restore signup and KYC while the vendor path is investigated.
actions.rationale: About half of KYC calls fail and orchestrator returns 503s to the signup flow; successful calls show the path is partially working, so retries may recover some traffic. Whether a fallback provider exists is not established in the evidence.

actions.text: Review egress/firewall, DNS and network policy changes for auth-kyc around 09:55 UTC, including infra changes the change tool does not record, and check the vendor endpoint/port configuration.
actions.rationale: The deploy/config/flag change tool shows no auth-kyc change near onset, so a non-recorded infra or vendor-side change is the remaining candidate.

actions.text: Verify the KYC provider credential and TLS certificate expiry dates as a low-cost check.
actions.rationale: Silent expiry is not visible in change history, so it cannot be ruled out, although the refused-connection error does not point to it.

actions.text: Add kyc-provider as a modelled dependency of auth-kyc, with a synthetic connectivity check and alerting on connection-refused errors.
actions.rationale: The topology showed no outgoing edges for auth-kyc, so the external dependency was invisible to the dependency graph.

actions.text: Add a circuit breaker/fallback in orchestrator for auth-kyc 503s, and alerting on auth-kyc error rate.
actions.rationale: The auth-kyc failure propagated to orchestrator as persistent 503s and an elevated error rate through 10:25.
